========== FILE: guides/reference/glossary.md ==========

[← Front page](../../README.md) &nbsp;·&nbsp; [Feedback form](https://forms.gle/k1pnQ4dtvfcGkuGK6)

# Glossary: flexibility, DERMS, interconnection, edge

Plain definitions. Terms with a source are from the deep research run
([catalog/research/edge-compute](../../catalog/research/edge-compute/README.md)); others are general usage.

## 1. Edge and data centers

| # | Term | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Edge data center | Small facility near users or data sources to cut latency, often kW to a few MW. No standard definition | general |
| 2 | MEC | Multi-access edge computing: cloud capabilities and an IT service environment at the network edge | https://www.etsi.org/technical-groups/mec/ |
| 3 | Hyperscale data center | Very large facility (often 100 MW+) run by a cloud or AI company | general |
| 4 | Power usage effectiveness (PUE) | Total facility energy divided by IT equipment energy | https://datacenters.lbl.gov/publications/avoiding-waste-heat-through-ai |
| 5 | Water usage effectiveness (WUE) | Annual onsite water use divided by IT energy, L/kWh-IT | https://datacenters.lbl.gov/sites/default/files/2023-07/DOE%20AM%20Tool--User%27s%20Manual%20v3.1%20%287-25-2023%29.pdf |
| 6 | Power capping | Limiting IT or facility power to an explicit maximum | https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2024-08/Powering%20AI%20and%20Data%20Center%20Infrastructure%20Recommendations%20July%202024.pdf |
| 7 | Temporal workload shifting | Moving a compute job to a different time with the same result | https://eta.lbl.gov/publications/integrating-ai-data-centers-power |
| 8 | Geographic workload shifting | Moving computation between sites or regions based on grid supply, price or carbon | https://eta.lbl.gov/publications/integrating-ai-data-centers-power |
| 9 | Voltage ride-through | Ability of equipment or load to stay connected through voltage disturbances instead of tripping | https://www.ercot.com/services/comm/mkt_notices/M-B062325-01 |
| 10 | Thermal energy storage | Storing heating or cooling so thermal demand can shift in time | https://www.energy.gov/oe/articles/microgrids-large-electric-loads-grid-support-how-leverage-microgrids-support-utilities |

## 2. Grid capacity and interconnection

| # | Term | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | Hosting capacity | Generation or load a grid location can take without significant upgrades or violations | https://www.pge.com/assets/pge/docs/about/doing-business-with-pge/pge-grip-user-guide.pdf |
| 12 | Integration Capacity Analysis (ICA) | California term for distribution hosting capacity analysis | same as above |
| 13 | Load ICA | Load a distribution line section can accept without significant upgrades | same as above |
| 14 | Limited generation profile | Time-varying export limit based on available hosting capacity | https://marketplace.sdge.com/more-information/customer-generation/enhanced-integration-capacity-analysis-ica |
| 15 | Flexible interconnection | Connection where injection or withdrawal can be limited dynamically instead of guaranteed firm | https://www.pge.com/assets/pge/docs/about/doing-business-with-pge/pge-grip-user-guide.pdf |
| 16 | Firm service | Service planned to meet a set load without routine curtailment for lack of network capacity | https://www.misoenergy.org/engage/MISO-Dashboard/firm-service-step-up-for-large-load-interconnections/ |
| 17 | Non-firm service | Service whose usable capacity may be restricted under defined grid conditions | same as above |
| 18 | Interconnection queue | List of projects waiting for grid connection studies; PJM has none for loads | https://insidelines.pjm.com/pjm-kicks-off-annual-process-of-vetting-large-load-requests/ |
| 19 | Large load | Load above a threshold that triggers special interconnection rules (ERCOT: 25 MW and up) | https://www.ercot.com/mktrules/issues/NPRR1234 |
| 20 | Load forecast | Estimate of future consumption or peak used for planning and procurement | https://learn.pjm.com/three-priorities/planning-for-the-future/load-forecasting |
| 21 | Local capacity requirement | Minimum capacity needed inside a constrained local transmission area | https://stakeholdercenter.prod.caiso.com/RecurringStakeholderProcesses/Local-capacity-requirements-process-2027 |
| 22 | Resource adequacy | Capacity procured so enough resources serve expected demand | https://www.caiso.com/generation-transmission/resource-adequacy |
| 23 | Capacity credit | Dependable share of nameplate capacity at times of need; equal MW is not equal reliability | https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2024-04/2024%20The%20Future%20of%20Resource%20Adequacy%20Report.pdf |
| 24 | Feeder | Distribution line from a substation to customers | general |
| 25 | Substation | Facility that changes voltage between transmission and distribution | general |
| 26 | ISO / RTO | Operator of the wholesale market and grid in a region (CAISO, ERCOT, PJM, MISO) | https://www.eia.gov/electricity/wholesalemarkets/ |
| 27 | Balancing authority | Entity balancing supply and demand in an area; EIA-930 reports by BA | https://www.eia.gov/electricity/930-content/about.html |
| 28 | LMP | Locational marginal price: wholesale price at a grid node | general |
| 29 | Capacity market | Market for commitments that enough future capacity will be available | https://insidelines.pjm.com/pjm-stakeholders-advance-initiatives-to-reliably-integrate-data-centers/ |
| 30 | Ancillary services | Services keeping the grid stable: regulation, reserves, frequency response | https://www.ferc.gov/ferc-order-no-2222-explainer-facilitating-participation-electricity-markets-distributed-energy |

## 3. Flexibility and DERMS

| # | Term | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 31 | DER | Small resource on the distribution system or behind a meter: storage, generation, responsive load | https://www.ferc.gov/ferc-order-no-2222-explainer-facilitating-participation-electricity-markets-distributed-energy |
| 32 | DER aggregation | Many DERs coordinated to provide a grid or market service together | same as above |
| 33 | DER aggregator | Entity that organizes DERs for participation in an RTO/ISO market | same as above |
| 34 | DERMS | Software that monitors, coordinates and can control DERs across a distribution grid | https://www.energy.gov/nepa/articles/cx-270851-alabama-power-company-distributed-energy-resources-management-system-derms |
| 35 | ADMS | Advanced distribution management system: utility operations, models and control | https://www.energy.gov/nepa/articles/cx-031615-adms-and-derms-initiative |
| 36 | VPP | Coordinated portfolio of distributed resources operated as one grid resource | https://www.energy.gov/technologycommercialization/articles/us-department-energy-releases-new-reports-highlighting |
| 37 | Demand response | Change in consumption in response to grid, price or program signals | https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/federal-demand-flexibility |
| 38 | Demand flexibility | Ability to shed, shift or modulate consumption | https://bies.lbl.gov/demand-flexibility |
| 39 | Load shedding | Temporarily reducing demand without moving it to another time | same as above |
| 40 | Load shifting | Moving consumption from one time to another | same as above |
| 41 | Load modulation | Repeatedly adjusting demand up or down rather than one shed event | same as above |
| 42 | Curtailable load | Demand that can be contractually reduced under set conditions | https://www.pge.com/en/save-energy-and-money/energy-saving-programs/demand-response-programs/business-programs.html |
| 43 | Proxy Demand Resource (PDR) | CAISO model letting aggregated demand reductions bid into the market | https://www.caiso.com/generation-transmission/load/demand-response |
| 44 | Reliability Demand Response Resource | CAISO DR resource dispatched for reliability | same as above |
| 45 | DER Provider (DERP) | CAISO participant operating a DER aggregation in wholesale markets | https://www.caiso.com/generation-transmission/generation/distributed-energy-resources |
| 46 | Behind-the-meter | On the customer side of the utility meter | https://stakeholdercenter.caiso.com/InitiativeDocuments/Straw-Proposal-and-Issue-Paper-Demand-and-Distributed-Energy-Market-Integration-Mar-13-2026.pdf |
| 47 | Carbon intensity | Emissions per unit of electricity, average or marginal | general |
| 48 | Marginal emissions (MOER) | Emissions from the generator that responds to the next unit of demand | https://watttime.org/data-science/data-signals/ |

## 4. Standards and rules

| # | Term | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 49 | FERC Order 2222 | Requires organized US markets to accept DER aggregations (minimum size up to 100 kW). Not ERCOT | https://www.ferc.gov/ferc-order-no-2222-explainer-facilitating-participation-electricity-markets-distributed-energy |
| 50 | OpenADR | Open standard for automated DR, price and grid-event signals | https://www.openadr.org/ |
| 51 | VTN | OpenADR Virtual Top Node: publishes programs and events | https://www.openadr.org/openadr-3-0 |
| 52 | VEN | OpenADR Virtual End Node: receives and responds to signals | same as above |
| 53 | IEEE 2030.5 | RESTful Smart Energy Profile for utility-to-device communication and DER control | https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/2030.5/11216/ |
| 54 | IEEE 1547 | Standard for DER interconnection and interoperability on distribution grids | https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1547/5915/ |
| 55 | PMU | Phasor measurement unit: synchronized measurement of phasors and frequency | https://www.misoenergy.org/engage/MISO-Dashboard/operational-reliability-requirement---large-load-telemetry-and-phasor-measurement-unit-pmu-requirements/ |
| 56 | ICCP | Inter-Control Center Communications Protocol for real-time telemetry between control centers | same as above |



========== FILE: guides/reference/data-setup.md ==========

[← Front page](../../README.md) &nbsp;·&nbsp; [Feedback form](https://forms.gle/k1pnQ4dtvfcGkuGK6)

# Data facts and setup cost (all tracks)

Facts about public siting data that affect what can be built in a day. Each row cites a catalog id.

## 1. Facts about the data

| # | Fact | Source id |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Detailed real grid models are restricted as Critical Energy/Electric Infrastructure Information; access needs a request and NDA | `ferc-ceii` |
| 2 | Public studies therefore use synthetic grids: realistic structure and similar load and generation, but no relation to the actual network at that location | `tamu-synthetic-grids` |
| 3 | The western US synthetic grid ships with substation coordinates, so a region can be cut out by a latitude/longitude box | `tamu-activsg10k` |
| 4 | The same package includes an N-1 branch contingency list but no hourly load series | `tamu-activsg10k` |
| 5 | The Texas synthetic grid includes a year of hourly load scenarios | `tamu-activsg2000` |
| 6 | Hourly load shapes for real regions come from balancing authority and ISO data | `eia-930`, `caiso-oasis`, `pjm-dataminer`, `gridstatus` |
| 7 | Utility hosting capacity maps are screening estimates under stated assumptions, not commitments | `pge-ica`, `pge-grip-guide`, `sce-drpep` |
| 8 | Hosting capacity maps cover distribution feeders; transmission constraints sit in ISO studies | `caiso-lcr-2027`, `ercot-constraints-2025` |
| 9 | Power flow answers whether the network physically carries a load (thermal and voltage limits); production cost models optimize dispatch and assume deliverability; capacity expansion models choose what to build | `pandapower`, `matpower`, `pypsa` |
| 10 | Reliability is usually measured across a full year (for example loss of load expectation), and equal MW does not give equal reliability | `doe-resource-adequacy-2024` |
| 11 | Measured data center load data is scarce in public; available proxies are load shape libraries, cluster power traces and simulated building loads | `epri-dcflex-deliverables`, `google-cluster-data`, `comstock` |
| 12 | OpenStreetMap power infrastructure is volunteer-mapped and uneven by region | `overpass-api`, `openinframap` |
| 13 | Large loads can trip offline together during grid faults; operators now ask for ride-through data | `pjm-load-transfer-event-2026`, `ercot-ride-through-notice` |

## 2. No key needed

| # | Resource | Gives you | Id |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Synthetic grids + MATPOWER / pandapower | Network to run power flow on | `tamu-activsg10k`, `matpower`, `pandapower` |
| 2 | Overpass API | Substations, lines, buildings from OSM | `overpass-api` |
| 3 | Census Reporter API | Population, income, housing by geography | `census-reporter-api` |
| 4 | Open-Meteo | Hourly weather by coordinate | `open-meteo` |
| 5 | EIA-930 bulk files | Hourly demand and generation by balancing authority | `eia-930` |
| 6 | CAISO OASIS / Today's Outlook | California prices, load, supply | `caiso-oasis`, `caiso-todays-outlook` |
| 6b | Grid Status website (browsing) | Prices, demand, fuel mix for every US ISO; API needs an account | `gridstatus-io` |
| 7 | PG&E GRIP (https://grip.pge.com/), SCE ICA FeatureServer | Feeder hosting capacity (California) | `pge-ica`, `pge-grip-guide`, `sce-ica-featureserver` |
| 8 | FEMA flood and risk data | Hazard exposure | `fema-nfhl`, `fema-nri` |
| 9 | Building footprints | Footprint polygons | `microsoft-us-building-footprints` |
| 10 | EAGLE-I outage history | County outages at 15-minute resolution | `eagle-i-outages` |
| 11 | Workload traces | Compute demand patterns | `google-cluster-data`, `azure-llm-inference-traces` |
| 12 | CPUC fire threat districts | Wildfire tiers (California) | `cpuc-fire-threat-map` |

`python3 scripts/find.py --track 1 --access open` lists all open resources for a track.

## 3. Needs a key, account or billing

| # | Resource | Setup | Id |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | EIA API v2 | Free key by email | `eia-api-v2` |
| 2 | Official Census API | Free key | `census-acs` |
| 3 | NOAA CDO | Free token, 10,000 requests/day | `noaa-cdo-api` |
| 4 | PJM Data Miner API | Free account | `pjm-dataminer` |
| 5 | Materials Project, NSRDB | Free key | `materials-project`, `nsrdb` |
| 6 | Electricity Maps, WattTime | Account; free tiers or trials with limits | `electricity-maps`, `watttime` |
| 7 | Google Earth Engine | Register a Cloud project (free non-commercial) | `google-earth-engine` |
| 8 | Google Solar API | Cloud project with billing and API key | `google-solar-api` |
| 9 | ERA5 | Copernicus account; download queue | `era5` |
| 10 | RIPE Atlas on BigQuery | Google account and project | `ripe-atlas` |

# SF x MIT Hack Day: Energy

| # | Item | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Date | Sunday 8 November 2026, 10:00 to 19:30 |
| 2 | Venue | AGI House SF, 170 St Germain Ave, San Francisco, CA 94114 |
| 3 | Format | One-day hack. Teams form at 10:30, demos at 18:30 |
| 4 | Theme | Grid-friendly compute |
| 5 | Questions about the repo | [Feedback form](https://forms.gle/k1pnQ4dtvfcGkuGK6) or arhams@stanford.edu |

## Schedule

| Time | Item |
|---|---|
| 10:00 | Doors, coffee, intro |
| 10:30 | Team formation |
| 13:00 | Lunch |
| 18:30 | Demos |
| 19:30 | Done |

## Event statement (verbatim)

> Expect to hack on compute energy infrastructure and grid capacity forecasting.
>
> A battery chemistry that lasts 20% longer or a grid model that predicts a failure an hour earlier
> is worth real money, and a lot of it can be tested in simulation before anyone touches hardware.
> We want agents that do that testing and get better at it each run.

## Tracks

| # | Track | Page |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Identify suitable sites | [tracks/1-sites](../../tracks/1-sites/README.md) |
| 2 | Assess grid capacity at the edge | [tracks/2-grid-capacity](../../tracks/2-grid-capacity/README.md) |
| 3 | Manage loads | [tracks/3-load-management](../../tracks/3-load-management/README.md) |
| 4 | Aggregate distributed compute | [tracks/4-aggregation](../../tracks/4-aggregation/README.md) |

The original event page also listed Materials for energy and Grid and fusion. Resources for those
are kept in [guides/reference/](../reference/README.md).

## Organisers

| # | Group | Description (from the event page) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | AGI House SF | Hacker house where researchers and founders build on the frontier. Hackathons, salons, dinners most weeks |
| 2 | Sundai Club | AI hacker community from Harvard and MIT. 130+ consecutive Sunday hacks, 1000+ projects |
| 3 | RSIhouse.ai | Weekly open space for hacks and dinners on recursive self-improvement |
| 4 | Autolab.ai | Infrastructure for RSI, starting with evals and autonomous continual learning |
| 5 | Superradiant | Research lab building self-improving agents for the sciences. Founders Micah Stubbs and Alejandro Zarzuelo Urdiales put this series together |
| 6 | Stanford Energy Club | Stanford's student-led energy organisation. Organised Stanford Climate Week (70+ events) |



========== CATALOG (one line per resource) ==========

a-lab-2023 | track - | paper | verified | Szymanski et al., An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of novel materials (Nature 2023) | https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06734-w | Robotic lab with computational targets and active learning; 41 of 58 targets synthesized in 17 days. Claims later disputed in the literature.
ac-grid-lab | track 2 | tool | open | AC Grid Lab (browser AC power flow) | https://www.eshansingh.xyz/acopf/ | Browser tool: build a one-line network on a map or diagram and solve AC power flow; starter case is a California-inspired nine-bus network with voltage and line-loading checks. JSON import and export.
acn-data | track 3,4 | dataset | registration | ACN-Data: EV charging sessions (Caltech) | https://ev.caltech.edu/dataset | Real EV charging sessions from Caltech, JPL and an office site: arrival, departure, energy requested and delivered. API with a free token.
acnportal | track 3,4 | simulator | open | acnportal / ACN-Sim (Caltech) | https://github.com/zach401/acnportal | Simulator for scheduling many EV chargers under site capacity limits, plus a client for ACN-Data. BSD-3.
afdc-stations | track 1,3 | dataset | open | AFDC alternative fuel station locator (US DOE) | https://afdc.energy.gov/stations | US public EV charging stations with location, network, connector types and power level. API through the NREL developer network (free key).
aflow | track - | dataset | open | AFLOW | https://aflow.org/ | High-throughput DFT database of millions of material entries with REST API.
ai-scientist | track - | tool | open | The AI Scientist (Sakana AI) | https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist | End-to-end loop that generates research ideas, runs experiments from templates and writes papers.

aideml | track - | tool | open | AIDE (Weco AI) | https://github.com/WecoAI/aideml | Agent that iterates on ML code with a tree search over solutions, scored by a user-defined metric.
alexandria | track - | dataset | open | Alexandria materials database | https://alexandria.icams.rub.de/ | Millions of DFT calculations of periodic compounds, used to train ML interatomic potentials.

alphaevolve-2025 | track - | paper | preprint | Novikov et al., AlphaEvolve (Google DeepMind, 2025) | https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13131 | LLM-driven evolutionary coding agent with automated evaluators; reported results in math, scheduling and kernel optimization.
andes | track 2,4 | simulator | open | ANDES: power system transient dynamics in Python (CURENT) | https://github.com/CURENT/andes | Python library for phasor-domain transient stability simulation with symbolic model definitions, including inverter-based resource models. See the repo for license.
ase | track - | tool | open | Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE) | https://gitlab.com/ase/ase | Python toolkit to set up, run and analyze atomistic simulations with many calculators, including ML potentials.

autoresearch | track - | tool | open | autoresearch (Andrej Karpathy) | https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch | Minimal loop where an agent edits a training script, runs a short experiment, and keeps changes that improve a validation metric.

No power, location or deadlines. CC BY.

bdg2 | track - | dataset | open | Building Data Genome Project 2 | https://github.com/buds-lab/building-data-genome-project-2 | Two years of hourly meter data from 1,636 non-residential buildings with weather and metadata. Used for load forecasting benchmarks.
bess-flexible-dispatch | track 3,2 | tool | open | Flexible BESS dispatch and arbitrage optimizer under grid constraints | https://github.com/Mohammadrezarefaei/bess-flexible-dispatch-optimizer | Optimizes battery charging and discharging across market prices while respecting hourly non-firm grid export limits and degradation cost. Example data from the German market. No clear license in the repo; ask before reusing code.
buildingsbench | track - | benchmark | open | BuildingsBench (NREL, now NLR) | https://github.com/NREL/BuildingsBench | Benchmark and 900k simulated buildings for short-term load forecasting, including zero-shot tests on real buildings.
ca-dr-potential-phase4 | track 3,4 | report | verified | LBNL / CPUC, California Demand Response Potential Study Phase 4 (2024) | https://eta.lbl.gov/publications/california-demand-response-0 | Shed and shift DR potential in California through 2050 by end use.
ca-dsgs | track 3,4 | program | verified | California Demand Side Grid Support (DSGS) program | https://www.energy.ca.gov/programs-and-topics/programs/demand-side-grid-support-program | Pays eligible customers for net load reduction and backup generation during extreme events, May to October. Fifth Edition guidelines adopted 27 Apr 2026.

caiso-demand-response | track 3,4 | program | verified | CAISO Demand Response participation | https://www.caiso.com/generation-transmission/load/demand-response | Proxy Demand Resource and Reliability DR Resource models. Needs a scheduling coordinator and revenue-quality meters; ancillary services need telemetry.
caiso-der-provider | track 3,4 | program | verified | CAISO Distributed Energy Resource Provider model | https://www.caiso.com/generation-transmission/generation/distributed-energy-resources | DER aggregations in wholesale markets. Utility concurrence review of 30 business days, then onboarding, metering and agreements.
caiso-dmm-dr-2024 | track 3,4 | report | verified | CAISO DMM, Demand Response Issues and Performance 2024 | https://www.caiso.com/documents/demand-response-issues-and-performance-2024-feb-20-2025.pdf | DR was about 1,400 MW, 2.6% of CAISO RA capacity in summer 2024; only 44% of utility PDR RA capacity was bid on high-load days.

watttime | track 3,4 | api | api-key | WattTime API | https://watttime.org/data-science/data-signals/ | Signals: co2_moer (marginal, lb/MWh), co2_aoer (average), health_damage (USD/MWh), with forecasts for load shifting. API docs could not be fetched in research; check access terms.
wecc240-2011 | track 2 | paper | verified | Price and Goodin, Reduced Network Modeling of WECC as a Market Design Prototype (IEEE PES 2011) | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/6039476 | Describes a 240-bus reduced Western Interconnection model built by CAISO staff, detailed inside California, with hourly load profiles for CAISO areas. Paywalled; the case file is not bundled with MATPOWER.
wind-toolkit | track - | dataset | api-key | NREL (now NLR) WIND Toolkit | https://www.nlr.gov/grid/wind-toolkit | Modeled wind speed and power for 126k US sites at 5-minute resolution, 2007 to 2013.
wri-aqueduct | track 1 | dataset | open | WRI Aqueduct water risk atlas | https://www.wri.org/aqueduct | Global water stress and water risk indicators by watershed. Relevant to cooling water availability.
